card.name: Haka
card.tagline: Aotearoa New Zealand — Māori chant and challenge. The ground itself answers.
card.profile: Haka (; singular and plural haka, in both Māori and New Zealand English) are a variety of ceremonial dances in Māori culture. A performance art, haka are often performed by a group, with vigorous movements and stamping of the feet with rhythmically shouted accompaniment. Haka have been traditionally performed by both men and women for a variety of social functions within Māori culture. They are performed to welcome distinguished guests, or to acknowledge great achievements, occasions, or funerals. Kapa haka groups are common in schools.
card.insight: Prince Alfred, the Duke of Edinburgh, was the first royal to visit New Zealand, in 1869. In September 2024, thousands gathered in Eden Park in Auckland to break the record of the largest haka performance.

observation.setting: Large assembly hall or chapel with wooden benches, arched wooden ceiling, and elevated stage at the front, filled with people in school uniform.
observation.dancers: Large group of young men and boys in uniform, filling the hall.
observation.formation_and_space: Participants stand in rows between and in front of wooden benches, facing the front stage.
observation.posture: Upright torso with knees bent into a low, wide stance, weight lowered.
observation.footwork: Stamping feet on the floor in rhythm with the chanting and chest/thigh slaps.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms swing, punch, slap thighs and chest, and make strong gestures with open palms or fists.
observation.hips_and_torso: Torso bounces with knee bends; occasional leans and sharp posture shifts.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Low level stance with bent knees; no jumps or turns visible.
observation.costume_and_props: Grey shirts, shorts, dark sweaters, blazers, and ties (school uniform).
observation.cannot_infer: Exact foot placement and individual weight shifts are obscured by the crowded benches and low camera angle.

signature_moments.what: Dancers chant loudly while rapidly slapping their thighs and chest with open hands in unison.
Dancers thrust their arms upward and outward with wide eyes and extended tongues while shouting.
Dancers punch forward with clenched fists while maintaining a deep knee bend and aggressive facial expressions.
